9.name: Code Review
9.subagent_prompt: You are reviewing PR #{pr_number} for a bug fix. Project: {project_path}. PR targets {pr_target_branch}. Step 0: Read .pipeline-state/*-diagnosis.md for the original diagnosis. Step 1: Run git diff {pr_target_branch}...HEAD, read changed files. Check docs/PULL_REQUEST_CHECKLIST.md if exists. Step 2: Cross-ref diagnosis vs fix — verify root cause was addressed, not just symptom. Step 3: Review for correctness, security (XSS, injection, secrets), testing (bug fix MUST have regression test), code quality, docs, perf. Flag auto-reject triggers. Step 4: Run project test suite, report pass/fail. Step 5: Decide APPROVE/REQUEST_CHANGES/COMMENT. Step 6 MANDATORY: Post review to GitHub with gh pr review {pr_number} --comment --body '<formatted review>'. If REQUEST_CHANGES use --request-changes. Save to pr/feedback/ if dir exists. Step 7: Output verdict. Step FINAL (MANDATORY, #36): you are read-only — restore the executor's working tree before returning. Capture your starting branch first (START=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)); on exit run `git checkout "$START"` and verify `git status --porcelain` is clean (`git restore --staged --worktree .` + `git clean -fd` (remove untracked files you created) if you dirtied it). NEVER leave the tree on {pr_target_branch} or with reverted/staged files — a build/scp the executor runs next would ship stale content.

checklist.action: read .pipeline-state/<branch>-diagnosis.md for diagnosis compliance check
git diff against target branch
load project PR checklist if exists (docs/PULL_REQUEST_CHECKLIST.md)
cross-ref diagnosis vs fix — root cause addressed
verify regression test exists for the bug fix
review: correctness, security, testing, quality, docs, perf

mutation-test the claims: for any row naming a production mechanism as its subject, delete or invert that mechanism and confirm the row FAILS. A mutation table must mark each entry APPLIED (executed, with observed failures) or PREDICTED (a claim) — PR #34 found two uncovered branches hiding in the PREDICTED column. Execute a sample of the PREDICTED entries; one that kills nothing is a coverage gap or an equivalent mutant, and you must say which. Driver hygiene: pass --continue AND clear the per-module test-results dirs between runs, or a failing early module leaves stale XML that is misattributed to the current mutation (#36).
check auto-reject triggers (per profile and generic: print vs logging, except:pass, no tests, phantom modules, stub code)
run full test suite, report pass/fail
post review to GitHub: gh pr review --comment with formatted checklist and findings
save to pr/feedback/ if directory exists

persist the mutation table to `.pipeline-state/<branch>-mutations.md` — a table that exists only in a subagent's report cannot be audited by a later stage, which is exactly how PR #34's uncovered branches survived Implementation.
output APPROVE/REQUEST_CHANGES/COMMENT

10.name: Review Verdict
10.note: Verdict is determined by the Code Review subagent above. If APPROVE, proceed to Merge. If REQUEST_CHANGES, fix issues, re-commit, re-push, re-run Code Review.

checklist.action: if REQUEST_CHANGES: fix issues, re-commit, re-push, re-run stage 9
if APPROVE: proceed to Merge

11.name: Merge PR
11.subagent_prompt: Merge PR #{pr_number} in {project_path}. Step 0: Run 'gh pr checks {pr_number}' — verify CI green. If pre-existing failure, document with gh pr comment before merging. Step 1: Run gh pr merge {pr_number} --squash --delete-branch. Do NOT run gh pr review --approve (GitHub blocks self-approval). Output PR_MERGED or MERGE_FAILED.

12.name: Retrospective
12.subagent_prompt: Write retrospective for bug fix: {task_description}. Project: {project_path}. PR #{pr_number}. Run 'gh pr view {pr_number} --json commits,title,body' to get PR details (branch deleted after merge). Rate quality 1-5, what went well, lessons learned, improvements. MANDATORY: Post retro as gh pr comment {pr_number} --body '<formatted retro with quality, lessons, improvements>'. MANDATORY: Append to .pipeline-log.md (create if needed, ensure in .gitignore). Your FINAL output line MUST be exactly 'RETRO_COMPLETE'. If this PR closes a milestone, end the retro with a consolidated carry-forward section listing every open item from all the milestone's PR retros, so /pipeline-retro starts from one list.
